h1:
5 Budget Stays
on Koh Kood, Trat
That We've Reviewed
heroSub: Five budget Koh Kood stays we've reviewed in depth — a bungalow on a hill over Ao Salat bay, a small village guesthouse near Klong Hin beach, a canal-side homestay with sunset views, an Italian-owned bungalow resort with great food near Klong Chao, and beachfront bungalows on the clear water of Bang Bao Bay. Prices start around ฿650–2,500/night.
introH2: 🏝️ What kinds of budget stays does Koh Kood have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Koh Kood has a reputation as an island of luxury resorts costing tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of baht, so many people assume a trip here means a heavy budget — but the truth is there are still stays in the few-hundred to low-thousand baht range tucked into the island's village life and quiet corners, and that's exactly what makes a budget Koh Kood trip more fun than you'd expect. Some are bungalows on a hill looking down over a bay and mangroves; some are small village guesthouses where the owner helps arrange your boat and transfers; some are canal-side homestays where you step off the boat almost straight into your room; and some are beachfront bungalows where you walk out the door and snorkel over coral right there. The mistake many people make is paying a budget price but expecting a beachfront resort, then feeling shortchanged. This article gathers 5 budget Koh Kood stays we've reviewed in depth — on the Ao Salat side, the Klong Hin area, Klong Mad, Ban Ngamkho, and Bang Bao Bay — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the good points and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Koh Kood has no public transport and no train. Getting to the island means a roughly 5–6 hour drive from Bangkok to the Trat ferry piers (Laem Sok / Laem Ngop), then a speedboat across to Koh Kood of about 1–1.5 hours. The areas in this article: Ao Salat — the east side, a fishing village, near the pier, quiet, about 10–13 km from the famous beaches · Klong Hin–Klong Phrao — a community area in the middle of the island, about 5 min drive to Klong Hin beach and Ao Taphao · Klong Mad–Laem Phrao — the west side, next to Klong Mad pier, canal-side with sunset views · Ban Ngamkho — about 800 m from Klong Chao beach · Bang Bao Bay — the south side, right on the clear-water beach · Almost none of them are beachfront, so you should rent a motorbike (around ฿250–300/day) to get around the island, and tell your stay in advance about your pier and transfers.

entries.name: Ao Salat View Koh Kood
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.7 · Small island bungalow near Ao Salat pier
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ao Salat village · about 1 km to Ao Salat pier
entries.addr: 13 Moo 6, Ban Ao Salat, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among the 5 budget Koh Kood stays we reviewed, if you measure by "genuine local feel," many reviews put Ao Salat View Koh Kood first — it's a guesthouse of brightly coloured bungalows on a small hill in Ao Salat village, on the island's northeast side, looking down over Ao Salat bay, a line of mangroves, and rows of moored fishing boats. It scores around 8.7 from a handful of reviews, and it's the cheapest in this article, starting around ฿750/night. What makes people fall for it is the genuine fishing-village quiet — after dark there's almost no noise but nature, and reviews agree that mornings are quiet enough to hear only birdsong. The highlight reviews mention most often is the free kayaks for paddling out to explore the bay and the mangroves near the stay, an experience the tourist-beach side can't offer. On the rooms, there's a point reviews stress: the difference between the older rooms on the road side and the newer Sea View rooms — foreign reviews agree it's well worth paying a little more for a Sea View room, because you get the bay view, a newer room, plus air-con, a fridge, Wi-Fi, and hot water. Service is another consistently praised point; the recurring words are that the owner and staff are friendly and helpful, advising on routes, arranging pickup from the pier, and lending out the kayaks. Honest caveats from the reviews: the stay sits on a hill on the east side with no sandy beach in front, the famous beaches like Klong Chao and Taphao are about 10–13 km away so you'll need to rent a motorbike to get around, the pool is small and better for a dip than serious swimming, and it's a small place that still doesn't have many OTA reviews. Best for budget travellers who want to experience Koh Kood quiet and genuinely local, and who are ready to rent a motorbike and explore the beaches on their own.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Go for a Sea View room if your budget allows, because the price difference is small but you clearly get the bay view and a newer room · Book or ask about motorbike rental in advance, and try kayaking through the mangroves in the morning when the water is calmest and quietest.
pros: Lovely bay view from the hill over Ao Salat, with genuine fishing-village quiet
Free kayaks to paddle the mangroves and the bay (a point reviews praise often)
Cheapest in this article, starting around ฿750/night · near Ao Salat pier
Friendly, helpful owner and staff (from the reviews)
cons: No sandy beach in front, famous beaches 10–13 km away, motorbike needed
Cheapest rooms on the road side are older with no open view, choose Sea View
Small stay, still few OTA reviews · small pool, better for a dip

entries.name: Kama Siri Koh Kood
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Hin area · about 5 min drive to Klong Hin beach–Ao Taphao
entries.addr: Rural Road 4017, Klong Hin area, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: On Koh Kood, known for beachfront resorts costing thousands to hundreds of thousands of baht, Kama Siri Koh Kood chose to play a different game — it's a small guesthouse and bungalow place of around 8 rooms/units in the community near Klong Hin–Klong Phrao beach, selling the lowest starting price in this article at around ฿650/night. Open since around 2013 and renovated in 2015, it scores around 8.3 on Trip.com from a modest number of reviews, but most of them lean positive on value and care. What guests mention most in agreement, and what becomes the real highlight, is the kind and helpful owner and staff — reviews agree they advise on places to go, coordinate speedboat schedules, arrange transfers, and what many mention especially is helping arrange boat and bus tickets back to Bangkok, which greatly cuts down the hassle of the multi-leg trip from Koh Kood, so many say it feels more like staying at a friend's place than checking into a hotel. The rooms come in several types, from Standard rooms, some with a shared bathroom, to Deluxe Bungalows and the Deluxe Tent — an air-conditioned tent with a private bathroom that gives a camping feel but stays comfortable. Honest caveats: the stay is in the community, not beachfront and with no pool, about 5 min drive from Klong Hin beach and Ao Taphao, so you'll need to rent a scooter to go swimming yourself; rooms are small with basic amenities to match the price, breakfast is charged separately, Wi-Fi may not be strong everywhere, and the small number of rooms fills up fast in high season. Best for budget travellers, backpackers, couples, and groups of friends who want to save on the room to spend on activities and food, and for people who want to experience the real community feel of Koh Kood rather than the resort bubble.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Make full use of the owner's help — tell them your arrival time so they can coordinate the boat schedule, transfers, and tickets back to Bangkok, because this is the strength reviews praise most · Check whether the room you choose has a private or shared bathroom; if you want privacy and air-con, go for the Deluxe Bungalow or Deluxe Tent.
pros: Lowest starting price in this article, around ฿650/night, great value for Koh Kood
Kind owner and staff who arrange boat & bus back to Bangkok (a highlight reviews praise)
Has a Deluxe Tent — air-conditioned with private bathroom · friendly atmosphere
About 5 min drive to Klong Hin beach–Ao Taphao · free Wi-Fi and parking
cons: Not beachfront and no pool, you must rent a scooter to reach the beach
Rooms small with basic amenities · some Standard rooms share a bathroom
Breakfast charged separately · few rooms fill fast · still few reviews on some platforms

entries.name: Klong Mad Good View Homestay
entries.badge: 🌅 Sunset view · Next to the pier
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Klong Mad/Laem Phrao area · next to Klong Mad pier ~80 m
entries.addr: 12 Moo 1, Ban Klong Mad, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among the budget Koh Kood stays we reviewed, if you measure by "newness and a step-off-the-boat-to-your-room location," Klong Mad Good View Homestay is the one most worth watching — it's a small homestay of just 7 rooms newly opened in 2025 at Ban Klong Mad, on the Laem Phrao side on the island's west, scoring around 8.7 from 19 reviews on Trip.com, with location and service standing out. The standout of the location is that it sits just about 80 m from Klong Mad pier — for people landing at this pier, you step from the pier straight to your room with no further drive, which is very convenient on an island where getting around isn't as easy as in town. The point real reviews mention so often it becomes its signature is the sunset view in front of the stay, which many say is beautiful enough to be the main reason they chose to stay, paired with a quiet canal-side and mangrove setting. Another charm you won't find at a typical resort is the shared kitchen for guests to cook themselves, with a shared microwave and fridge; many choose to buy fresh seafood from the Klong Mad villagers to cook on their own, plus kayaking in the canal and squid fishing. Because it just opened, the rooms and amenities are still fairly new and clean, and several reviews praise the cleanliness and the friendliness of the owner who helps arrange tours and car rental. Honest caveats from the reviews: the stay is canal-side and near the pier, not on a sandy beach, so you need a vehicle to go swimming at the island's beaches, there's no pool, it's a small and simple homestay to match the price, some reviews mention the breakfast variety and certain cleanliness details that still need improvement, and because it's canal-side with mangroves you may at times encounter natural insects. Best for budget couples, small families, and travellers who like quiet, canal-side nature, and outdoor activities, using it as a base to explore around the island.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The stay has only 7 rooms, so availability is very limited; if your dates are set, book early · Tell the stay in advance which pier you'll land at and coordinate the transfer (late arrivals need 24 hours' notice) · Try buying fresh seafood from the villagers to cook in the shared kitchen, and rent a motorbike through the stay to go swimming.
pros: About 80 m from Klong Mad pier, step off the boat straight to your room
Lovely sunset view in front of the stay (a signature reviews praise) · quiet setting
New stay (opened 2025), clean rooms · has a shared kitchen to cook fresh seafood
Kind, friendly owner who arranges tours and car rental · kayaking/squid fishing
cons: Canal-side, not on a sandy beach, you need a vehicle to go swimming
No pool · it's a small 7-room homestay with limited availability
Breakfast not yet varied, service needs improvement at times (from reviews)

entries.name: Big Dreams Resort Koh Kood
entries.revCount: TripAdvisor 4/5 · 73 reviews · #9 specialty lodging Koh Kood
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Ngamkho · about 10–15 min walk to Klong Chao beach
tags: 🤝 Owner looks after you like a friend
entries.addr: 42/5 Moo 2, Ban Ngamkho, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: If the other budget stays in this article sell views and quiet, Big Dreams Resort Koh Kood chose to sell something different — the food and the owner. It's a small bungalow resort of just 6 units at Ban Ngamkho, near Klong Chao beach, run family-style by an Italian owner named Matteo and his Thai wife, starting around ฿1,100/night, scoring around 8.4 (TripAdvisor 4/5 from 73 reviews, ranked #9 among specialty lodging on Koh Kood). The most praised point, and what gives this small stay a reputation beyond its size, is the restaurant where the owner cooks himself, serving both home-style Thai food and freshly made Italian-Western dishes, from homemade pasta, pizza, and steak to fresh seafood; many reviews mention the pasta and steak as genuinely good and made fresh every plate. This matters especially because on Koh Kood the restaurants are spread far apart and getting around in the evening isn't convenient, so having a tasty kitchen at the resort is a real advantage — no need to go far to find dinner. Another heart of the place is owner Matteo, whom many reviews name and praise for looking after guests like people he knows, from handling pier transfers and helping book diving trips to recommending places and sitting down to chat with guests at dinner, so many say it feels like staying at a friend's place. Honest caveats from the reviews: the stay is in the Ban Ngamkho area, not beachfront, so you walk about 10–15 min (around 800 m) to Klong Chao beach, there's no pool, Wi-Fi covers only the common area and doesn't reach the rooms, the water pressure is low and at times water and power cut out as island conditions go, rooms are basic, the beds are fairly firm, there's no in-room fridge, and the restaurant prices look a touch high against the budget-stay image. Best for budget travellers, couples who aren't after luxury, and small families using the resort as a base to head out to the beach, diving, and motorbiking, then come back for a good dinner.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Try dinner at the resort's restaurant, because the food is the star here · Plan around the Wi-Fi that's only in the common area; if you need internet, bring a mobile data SIM · Rent a motorbike at the resort to get around the island, and if you come as a group, the Family or Quadruple Room is the best value.
pros: Fresh Thai-Italian food praised in almost every review (pasta, steak, seafood)
Italian owner looks after guests like a friend, helps arrange diving trips & pier transfers
Among the most affordable prices on the island · near Klong Chao beach & waterfall
Small 6-room stay with attentive care, friendly family atmosphere
cons: Not beachfront, about 10–15 min walk to Klong Chao beach · no pool
Wi-Fi only in the common area, doesn't reach the rooms · water/power cut out at times
Basic rooms, fairly firm beds, no in-room fridge (from reviews)

entries.name: Koh Kood Resort
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.2 · about 67 reviews · Beachfront bungalows on Bang Bao Bay
entries.badge: 🐠 On clear-water beach · Snorkel in front of the resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Bao Bay, south side of Koh Kood · beachfront
tags: 🐠 Snorkel in front of the resort
entries.addr: 45 Moo 5, Bang Bao Bay, Ko Kut, Trat
entries.storyHtml: Among the 5 budget Koh Kood stays we reviewed, Koh Kood Resort is the only one that's "truly beachfront" — it's a long-standing beachfront bungalow resort on Bang Bao Bay, on the island's south side, a crescent-shaped bay many rate as one of the clearest-water bays on the island, starting around ฿2,500/night, scoring 8.2 from about 67 reviews. What guests mention most is the snorkelling right in front of the resort, which you can do without taking a boat out far — at Bang Bao Bay there's a shallow coral reef just about one to five metres under the surface with schools of fish, so you simply walk from your bungalow to the beach, put on a mask, and get in the water. The beach is soft sand sloping gently into the sea with no strong rip currents, so it's safe for taking children into the water; there are floating beds along the shore, an outdoor pool for those who don't want to go in the sea, and the sunset view from the beachfront bar is a highlight reviews mention often. Another consistently praised point is the beachfront SeaView restaurant, which many say has food and cocktails better than expected, especially the seafood menu, which matters a lot on an island where going out to eat in the evening isn't convenient. Honest caveats from the reviews: some bungalows are starting to show their age and maintenance could improve, with people mentioning firm or sagging mattresses, damp, and stains on the walls in some units; the condition of each bungalow varies quite a bit; music from the bar/pool is loud until around 9–10 pm on some nights; service is slow at times when it's busy; and there are some extra charges as island-resort conditions go. Best for couples and families who want a beachfront Koh Kood stay, clear sea, and snorkelling in front of the resort at an affordable price, and who are ready to choose a good room and set expectations to match a small-island resort.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a sea-view room or a more recently renovated type, and check the latest photos and reviews before booking, because the condition of each bungalow varies a lot · If you're a light sleeper, ask for a room far from the bar and pool · Bring your own mask and snorkel, because the snorkelling spot is right in front of the resort.
pros: Truly beachfront, very clear sea in front, snorkel and see coral and fish right away
Bang Bao Bay's curve is lovely and quiet, with floating beds · sunset view at the bar
Has a beachfront pool · restaurant and cocktails praised as tasty
A Koh Kood beachfront stay at a more affordable starting price than luxury resorts
cons: Some bungalows are getting old, firm/sagging mattresses, damp (choose a good room)
Music/DJ from the beachfront bar runs late on some nights
Service slow at times when busy · the highest starting price in this article

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard-room range and may change by date and season; we recommend checking the real price and comparing 3 sites before every booking · The scores and highlights in this article come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms, not from staying ourselves · Many small stays on Koh Kood have few OTA reviews, so the scores should be read as a trend rather than a fixed number · Koh Kood has no public transport, and 4 of the 5 stays in this article are not beachfront, so you should rent a motorbike (around ฿250–300/day) to get around the island, and bring cash, mosquito repellent, and your own personal items, because shops and ATMs on the island are limited · In high season (November–April) the sea is clear and the weather is good, rooms fill fast, so book ahead · In the rainy season (May–October) many stays on the island close and boats run less often, so confirm opening dates and boat schedules with your stay before booking · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about budget Koh Kood stays

faq.q: ❓ How much do budget stays on Koh Kood start at?
faq.a: In this article, prices start around ฿650–2,500 per night · The cheapest is Kama Siri from ฿650 (a village guesthouse, some rooms with a shared bathroom) and Ao Salat View from ฿750 (a bay-view bungalow) · In the low-thousands are Klong Mad Good View ฿900 and Big Dreams Resort ฿1,100 · And the only truly beachfront one, Koh Kood Resort, starts at ฿2,500 · All prices are approximate starting prices from standard rooms; in high season prices may run higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best budget Koh Kood stay?
faq.a: It depends on your travel style · By review score, Ao Salat View and Klong Mad Good View tie at 8.7, the highest in this article · If you focus on saving the most and on owner care, Kama Siri from ฿650 · If you want good food, Big Dreams Resort, where the Italian owner cooks himself · And if you want to sleep beachfront and snorkel right away, Koh Kood Resort on the clear water of Bang Bao Bay.

faq.q: ❓ Are budget Koh Kood stays beachfront, and do I need to rent a vehicle?
faq.a: Most are not beachfront · 4 of the 5 (Ao Salat View, Kama Siri, Klong Mad Good View, Big Dreams) are on a hill, in the community, or canal-side, so you travel out to the beach yourself · Only Koh Kood Resort is directly on Bang Bao Bay beach · Because Koh Kood has no public transport, renting a motorbike (around ฿250–300/day) is almost a necessity if you stay in a non-beachfront area.

faq.q: ❓ How do you get to Koh Kood?
faq.a: From Bangkok, take a car or van to the Trat ferry piers (Laem Sok or Laem Ngop), about 5–6 hours, then a speedboat across to Koh Kood of about 1–1.5 hours · Boats dock at several piers (e.g. Ao Salat, Klong Mad), then you continue by car on the island to your stay · We recommend telling your stay in advance which pier you'll land at and coordinating the transfer, especially if you arrive in the evening — many of the small stays in this article can help arrange the boat and car.

faq.q: ❓ When is the best time to visit Koh Kood, and how far ahead should I book?
faq.a: The best time to visit Koh Kood is high season (November–April), with clear sea and good weather · Most of the budget stays in this article are small (6–8 rooms, some just 7), so they fill fast — book 3–6 weeks ahead or more in high season · In the rainy season (May–October) many stays on the island close and boats run less often, so confirm opening dates and boat schedules with your stay before booking, and choose Free Cancellation if your plans aren't set, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.

faq.q: ❓ Do budget Koh Kood stays have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: It varies · Koh Kood Resort has a beachfront pool, and Ao Salat View has a small hilltop pool (good for a dip) · Meanwhile Kama Siri, Klong Mad Good View, and Big Dreams have no pool · As for breakfast, many charge it separately or include it depending on the package, so check when booking · A highlight of some small stays is a shared kitchen for cooking yourself (Klong Mad) or an on-site restaurant that's praised (Big Dreams, Koh Kood Resort).
